title: Verdict and Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster Paloma Coldharbour has spent twelve years documenting the 1993 disappearance of a girl named Wren Ashby, the coldest case in the coastal town of Saltmere. When an anonymous confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the funeral of the town's beloved retired sheriff, Paloma realizes the letter's author knows details never made public — and that his own late father, once the sheriff's deputy, may be implicated. As Paloma peels back thirty-year-old alibis, he discovers the town's founding families built their loyalty on a shared lie, and that the 'found family' who raised him after his father's death were its architects. In the end, Paloma must choose between protecting the people who became his family and broadcasting the truth: Wren died accidentally during a night gone wrong, and the cover-up — not a killer — is Saltmere's real crime; he airs the final episode, and the tide finally gives up what it took.
about_author: Jude Blackwood is the pen name of a former court reporter who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. They live on a fog-bound coastline that supplies most of their atmosphere and none of their alibis.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet him cataloguing twelve years of case files in his cluttered studio above the bait shop, introducing his podcast 'Coldharbour' and his ritual of keeping Saltmere's secrets filed and alphabetized. The chapter ends with the arrival of an envelope postmarked the day after Sheriff Danvers's funeral. Emotional beat: lonely devotion cracked open by dread.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He reads the confession letter: 'I was there when Wren Ashby went into the water. Ask the widow.' The handwriting is unnervingly familiar. He cross-references details only the true witness could know. Emotional beat: the thrill of a lifetime colliding with the fear that this letter was meant for him specifically.

chapters.title: The Widow's Parlor
chapters.summary: Paloma interviews Marion Danvers, the sheriff's widow, whose grief curdles into warning: 'Some cases stay closed because opening them kills.' She slips him one name — Deputy Elias Coldharbour, Paloma's own father. Emotional beat: the floor giving way beneath the investigator.

chapters.title: A Boy and His Badge
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, alternating Paloma's present narration with reconstructed 1993 scenes from his father's perspective as a young deputy first assigned to the Ashby disappearance. Emotional beat: falling in love with a father he barely remembers, knowing where it leads.

chapters.title: The Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV with his researcher friend Noor, his found-family anchor. Together they map the official timeline against tidal records and find a six-hour gap everyone protected. Emotional beat: two friends realizing they've stopped chasing a story and started hunting their neighbors.

chapters.title: Alibi, Stitched
chapters.summary: Paloma interviews three of the town's founding families, each reciting identical alibis like rehearsed scripture. He notices the same phrase repeated word-for-word across thirty years. Emotional beat: creeping horror at how well-kept the lie is.

chapters.title: What the Bait Shop Knows
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She digs into property records and finds the founding families quietly bought up the shoreline where Wren vanished weeks after her disappearance. Emotional beat: loyalty to Paloma tested against her instinct to publish independently.

chapters.title: The Funeral Nobody Mourned
chapters.summary: Paloma attends the reading of Sheriff Danvers's will and discovers a sealed envelope addressed to 'whoever finishes my work.' The lawyer refuses to release it without proof of identity — or threat. Emotional beat: grief weaponized, suspicion blooming toward everyone he grew up respecting.

chapters.title: Letters to My Son
chapters.summary: Paloma opens his father's old footlocker and finds unsent letters describing the night Wren died — cut off mid-sentence, the final page missing. Emotional beat: a son hearing his father confess in fragments and begging the paper for more.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Swam Out
chapters.summary: Reconstructed 1993 night from multiple unreliable POVs gathered from interviews: bonfire, drinking, a dare, a storm rolling in. Each account contradicts the others in the same suspicious places. Emotional beat: the reader feels the truth assembling itself out of lies.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Paloma receives a cease-and-desist from the founding families' attorney — an old mentor who taught him everything about evidence. The message is clear: stop, and be cared for; continue, and be alone. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made literal in an offer.

chapters.title: Noor's Line in the Sand
chapters.summary: Noor confronts Paloma: she's found proof the sheriff falsified the original report, but publishing burns every bridge either of them has. They fight about whether truth belongs to the teller or the town. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under the weight of the case.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Paloma traces his father's final letter page to Marion Danvers, who kept it for thirty years as insurance. It names not a killer but four witnesses who stood on the shore and did nothing while Wren drowned. Emotional beat: relief and devastation — no monster, just complicity.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Paloma identifies the anonymous letter writer through handwriting analysis: it's the town doctor, now dying, who was the fifth person on the shore and the only one whose conscience survived. Emotional beat: mercy meeting accountability in a hospice room.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: The doctor's full account: Wren slipped from the rocks during the dare; the others fled; the sheriff, arriving late, chose reputation over rescue and stitched the alibis himself. Paloma's father wrote the truth and was silenced. Emotional beat: understanding the machinery of silence from inside it.

chapters.title: The Offer Withdrawn
chapters.summary: The founding families escalate: Paloma's lease is terminated, his sources dry up, and Noor is offered her dream job if she walks away. One by one, the town shows him exactly what exile looks like. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening resolve into something harder than anger.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: After a winter storm, erosion exposes remains and a locket on the shoreline below the founding families' properties. The police — still loyal to old names — move slowly. Paloma photographs everything before they can. Emotional beat: the sea testifying at last.

chapters.title: Episode Ninety-Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma records the penultimate episode laying out the entire architecture of the cover-up, holding it unpublished as leverage and as a final chance for the town to come forward voluntarily. Two of the four witnesses do. Emotional beat: the terrible power of an unplayed card.

chapters.title: The Widow's Choice
chapters.summary: Marion Danvers publicly releases her husband's sealed will-envelope, which contains his own written confession and the missing context: he acted to protect the town's only hospital funding, tied to the founding families. Emotional beat: grief transformed into the bravest act in the book.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Climax. Paloma publishes Episode 100. The town erupts; the surviving witnesses face charges; the founding families' attorney resigns mid-betrayal and hands over documents. Paloma stands in the courthouse square as the truth becomes undeniable. Emotional beat: catharsis earned at the cost of everything comfortable.

chapters.title: Alibi
chapters.summary: Resolution. At Wren Ashby's memorial, the town that shunned Paloma begins, imperfectly, to return — Noor beside him, the doctor's daughter thanking him. His father's last unfinished letter gets its ending read aloud. Emotional beat: found family re-forged on honest ground.

chapters.title: Filed Under W
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Paloma's POV. He closes the Ashby file and starts a new one labeled simply 'Saltmere' — because a town built on one lie keeps others. The final image: the tide coming in clean over the rocks. Emotional beat: vigilance tempered by peace.
